Notes rewritten to say so; the Hearst-specific unit count and street address were removed. The arcCA Digest page and the Regents item were added to source_doc_urls. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson and DataSF's Assessor tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 (675 Mission Bay Blvd in the repo's DataSF parcels copy) alone is about 12.2 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.'; notes: 'Part of a single UCSF Mission Bay student housing complex (Hearst Tower plus North, West and South/Student Housing buildings; the building names come from UCSF's housing-office page, which could not be read in the 2026-09 audit) -- UC's Block 20 Housing and Retail Project: four buildings totaling 298,800 sq ft housing more than 750 UCSF students, postdoctoral scholars and their families around a shared courtyard (Langan). The November 2002 UC Regents item anticipated full occupancy by October 2005; no source read states the actual opening. Architect Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) with Fisher Friedman Associates (arcCA Digest: 'student apartment complex by SOM with Fisher-Friedman'). This building: the North Building, 525 Nelson Rising Lane (OpenStreetMap), a 7-10 story mid-rise.'. 2026-10-12 TEXT CORRECTION (no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type): accuracy_caveat no longer calls the OpenStreetMap footprint 'surveyed' (OSM is volunteer-mapped; this way carries no source tag) and its example parcel was replaced: lot 8711507 (675 Mission Bay Blvd) does not contain this building, which lies in active lot 8711509 (roll lot area 528,539 sq ft, about 12.1 acres). notes: the capacity is no longer given as Langan's 'more than 750' alone, because the 2002 Regents item (a plan) says 717 students and postdoctoral scholars and the family of one manager and arcCA Digest says '760-bed'; the architect is no longer given as SOM with Fisher Friedman alone, because Langan's project page lists 'Architect Verde Design, Inc.' for the same four-building complex (no source read says how the two relate, so none is chosen); arcCA's wording was misquoted as 'student apartment complex by SOM with Fisher-Friedman' and is now quoted exactly ('A 760-bed student apartment complex, by SOM with Fisher Friedman'). The 298,800 sq ft total is confirmed by both Langan ('298,800 SF') and the Regents item ('298,800 residential asf').
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- OpenStreetMap building footprint (crowd-mapped, not an official survey), not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (in DataSF's Assessor parcel data the active lot 8711509 is about 12.2 acres by its drawn outline (the Assessor roll lists it at 555 Mission Bay Blvd with a lot area of 528,539 sq ft, about 12.1 acres) and contains this building together with the Hearst Tower, West and Diller buildings), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.
properties.notes: Part of a single UCSF Mission Bay student housing complex (Hearst Tower plus North, West and South/Student Housing buildings; the building names come from UCSF's housing-office page, which could not be checked in September 2026) -- UC's Block 20 Housing and Retail Project: four buildings totaling 298,800 sq ft around a shared courtyard (Langan; the November 2002 UC Regents item gives 298,800 residential assignable sq ft). Capacity differs by source: Langan says the buildings house "more than 750 UCSF students, postdoctoral scholars, and their families"; the 2002 Regents item, a plan, says "It will house 717 students and postdoctoral scholars and the family of one manager"; arcCA Digest calls the complex a "760-bed student apartment complex". The November 2002 UC Regents item anticipated full occupancy by October 2005; no source read states the actual opening. The architect is given differently: arcCA Digest says the complex is "by SOM with Fisher Friedman" (Skidmore, Owings & Merrill with Fisher Friedman), while Langan's project page lists "Architect Verde Design, Inc."; no source read says how the two relate, so none is chosen. This building: the North Building, 525 Nelson Rising Lane (OpenStreetMap), a 7-10 story mid-rise.
